title: From Headset to Pitch: Virtual Reality Adoption and Player Education in Greek Football Clubs
content: Virtual reality (VR) is increasingly promoted for perceptual-cognitive training in football, but its integration by clubs outside Europe's elite is little studied. This exploratory study examines three Greek professional clubs at different stages of adoption: AEK Athens FC, which introduced VR-based cognitive training in 2024, and two clubs that have not adopted it. Data comprised 13 public documents and an online staff survey (n = 13 of approximately 30 invited), interpreted against four European reference cases through a three-lens framework of learning, pedagogy and organisation. Most respondents expected VR to be useful and easy to use, and all agreed that VR should be linked to the club's game model, mediated by coach feedback and evaluated with university partners. Lack of specialised staff was the most frequently named barrier (12 of 13), and respondents at non-adopting clubs were more sceptical about transfer to the pitch and about cost. At the adopting club, staff described use across squads but infrequent personal involvement and differing views on how VR is evaluated. Positive acceptance of VR thus coexists with uncertainty about its integration into coaching and its evaluation. The study proposes a provisional integration typology, including a pre-adoption level, and recommendations for resource-limited clubs.
